messages:
jin: Heads-up — saw a short but sharp latency hitch in eu-west-3 around 12:40 UTC. p95 jumped ~60-80ms for ~3m.
ops-bot: ALERT: router-handoff-failure eu-west-3 shard=42 fallback=dedicated rate=0.62
jin: correlates with a flurry of tiny allocations + kvcache misses. stack shows a bunch of backfills and immediate handoffs.
sasha: I pulled the router logs — lot of `HandoffInit` -> `HandoffAbort` loops for requests < 512 tokens. looks like prefill race.
tayler: weird, we rolled a smaller-affinity tweak yesterday night (soft-affinity-v2). could be that.
marc: which rollout exactly? helen: deploy bot says `soft-affinity-v2` at 2026-03-15T06:03Z.
jin: that matches window. idea: either raise prefill delay for small requests or debounce handoff signals at the router.
sasha: raising prefill delay kills cold-start quality for some jobs. but the router debounce seems cheaper operationally.
tayler: we tried a 3s debounce in the past and it masked real failures. smaller window might work: try 500ms?
marc: +1 on 500ms. also tag fallback route so dedicated uses `kvcache_warm=true` for first few seconds. avoids repeated misses.
helen: cost hit? dedicated with warm tag could take a bit more tokens while warm, but prevents long tail latency for many users. tradeoff seems acceptable.
ops-bot: NOTE: runbook link updated: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/handoff-debounce.
jin: quick canary plan: set `handoff_debounce_ms=500` on eu-west-3 routers for 2 hours, enable `kvcache_warm=true` for fallback, monitor p95 and requestrate.
sasha: I'll watch dashboards. if p95 drops we'll bake.
tayler: I'll apply the debounce to the canary pool in 5m; posting command snippet: ```bash
# canary debounce update
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/routers/eu-west-3/canary/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"handoff_debounce_ms":500}'
```
marc: also adding a short alert suppressor for repeated handoff alerts in the next 30m to avoid paging noise.
ops-bot: ALERT SUPPRESS: handoff-loop-eu3 suppressed for 30m by marc.
sasha: 2m after canary: p50 stable, p95 down from ~220ms to ~160ms. error-rate unchanged. :thumbsup:
jin: looks promising. if steady at 2h we can rollout region-wide and add a note in the cost dashboard for the small dedicated-warm cost.
helen: please add a postmortem-lite to the infra board explaining root cause + rollback steps.
tayler: will do. thanks all.
